title: Advanced Error Analysis and Sentence Reconstruction
orientation: Advanced editing requires you to solve unfamiliar problems and to recognise when no correction is needed. This lesson combines agreement, reference, complement patterns, modifiers, scope and paragraph grammar without assuming that every sentence contains exactly one fault. You will record the intended meaning, diagnose each relationship, propose a defensible repair and test the consequences of that repair. Earlier structures return in deliberately varied contexts, including formal inversion, British collective agreement and embedded questions that can look suspicious. The reconstruction activities ask you to combine, split and reorder sentences while preserving participants, time, modality and logical relationships. Open responses include model analyses and specific rubrics; an alternative wording can be fully valid. The aim is controlled judgement, not automatic substitution or obedience to an unsupported examiner preference. When context cannot determine an intended reading, make the uncertainty explicit and show conditional alternatives.
outcomes: Recognise suspicious but grammatical structures in context.
Use a meaning ledger for transformations.
Revise sentences and paragraphs without adding certainty or changing reference.
Explain corrections, exceptions and alternative solutions with evidence.

modules.title: Diagnose the relationship before changing the words
modules.definition: Grammatical error analysis identifies a problematic relationship, explains the applicable construction and checks whether a proposed repair is supported by the intended meaning. An unusual form is not itself proof of an error.
foundation: Read the complete context before selecting a correction. Identify the main clauses, their subjects and finite verb phrases, then examine the relationships inside them. In The quality of the reports have improved, quality is the singular head of the subject and has is the conventional agreement repair. In The reports have improved in quality, the plural verb is already correct. The same vocabulary therefore supports different grammatical analyses. State the relationship that fails rather than pointing to the nearest unfamiliar word.
intermediate: Separate a confirmed error from missing information. In Amina told Salma that her proposal was accepted, her can refer to either woman unless context settles the reference. The sentence is not structurally ungrammatical, but a report may need explicit naming. In The committee have submitted their views, British member-oriented agreement is possible, so a correction to has/its must be justified by intended unit reference or a specified editorial system. A diagnostic note should say whether the issue is agreement, reference, scope, complementation, punctuation, meaning or register.
advanced: Some sentences contain more than one fault. The findings was presented very clear contains plural-subject agreement and an adjective–adverb problem for the intended description of presentation. Repairing only was leaves the second issue. Conversely, changing every marked expression can introduce errors or change tone unnecessarily. Use a staged record: original wording, intended meaning, diagnosed relation, minimum adequate repair, alternative repair and limiting exception. Minimum means sufficient to solve the stated problem, not always the fewest written characters or an obligation to retain a misleading structure.
expert: Evidence-sensitive analysis remains open to alternative frameworks. Traditional accounts may call an -ing construction a gerund phrase where a modern account analyses a non-finite clause. If both identify the same form, internal subject relationship and external function, terminology alone need not invalidate an answer. When authorities differ, ask whether they describe different registers, national conventions, senses or theoretical categories. Do not invent a source citation to make a judgement look final. Where context supports more than one correction, list the alternatives and state which meaning each preserves.

patterns.form: context → structure → disputed relationship → repair → verification
patterns.meaning: Makes the reasoning behind an edit explicit.

patterns.form: one sentence → possibly several independent diagnoses
patterns.meaning: A task may contain multiple genuine faults; identify each rather than stopping automatically after one.

examples.sentence: The list of entries is incomplete.
examples.analysis: Singular list controls is despite plural entries inside the of-phrase.

examples.sentence: The officer found the account convincing.
examples.analysis: Convincing functions as an object complement describing the account.

examples.sentence: The committee have discussed their individual objections.
examples.analysis: Member-oriented British agreement is defensible; unfamiliar plural agreement is not enough to prove error.

contrasts.a: The findings were presented very clearly.
contrasts.note: Both are grammatical but different: the first describes presentation manner; the second describes the findings themselves.

exceptions: A grammatical sentence can still be ambiguous, misleading or unsuitable for an audience. Diagnose that actual problem instead of inventing a syntactic fault.

mistakes.problem: The number of visitors have increased.
mistakes.repair: The number of visitors has increased.
mistakes.reason: Number heads a singular measure expression here.

mistakes.repair: She explained the procedure to me.
mistakes.reason: Explain takes the topic as direct object and ordinarily marks this recipient with to.

glossary.definition: An evidence-based explanation of a problematic grammatical relationship.
An unnecessary change that treats a defensible construction as faulty.

modules.title: Reconstruction with a meaning ledger
modules.definition: A meaning ledger records the information a transformation must preserve: participants, event, time, polarity, quantity, modality and logical relationship. Reconstruction changes form while checking these features explicitly.
foundation: Start with who did what, when and with what degree of commitment. Hana may submit the report tomorrow does not mean Hana will submit it, and Hana did not submit it does not mean that nobody did. When combining sentences, choose a connector justified by the source: The lights failed. The session ended early permits a simple and combination without proving that one caused the other. A because combination needs a supplied causal relationship. Sentence splitting must preserve a concession, condition or limitation rather than leaving two loosely associated claims.
intermediate: Transformations offer several structural resources: active and passive voice, finite and non-finite clauses, relative clauses, nominalisation, coordination and marked order. Each has restrictions. A passive normally needs a compatible verb construction, and it must retain an identified agent when that identity matters. The assessor rejected the appeal can become The appeal was rejected by the assessor. A shortened The appeal was rejected omits the named actor, so it may be unsuitable in an exact-content transformation. Fronting or clefting may preserve the central proposition while adding focus or a presuppositional effect.
advanced: Word-order reconstruction requires hierarchy, not just arranging familiar neighbours. Identify which words form a noun phrase, which auxiliaries precede the lexical verb and which clause a modifier belongs to. Only the clerk checked the forms and The clerk checked only the forms place the focus restriction on different constituents. Keep a negative with the intended scope. Not all candidates passed allows some passes; no candidates passed excludes every pass. If a transformation silently exchanges these, grammatical fluency cannot repair the changed meaning.
expert: After writing a candidate reconstruction, compare its entailments with the source. Decided to leave does not entail left; advised her to leave does not entail that she obeyed; failed to leave does entail that the intended leaving did not occur. Avoid replacing an uncertain source with an authoritative-sounding nominalisation such as the proven failure. Some tasks demand only preservation of a central proposition, while others require close semantic equivalence. State which standard applies, especially when an inversion, cleft, nominalisation or passive changes emphasis, reference accessibility or assumed background.

patterns.form: source proposition + ledger → reconstructed structure + ledger check
patterns.meaning: Tests meaning as well as formal correctness.

patterns.form: not all X → partial negation; no X → total exclusion
patterns.meaning: The two quantificational claims are not equivalent.

examples.sentence: The appeal was rejected by the assessor.
examples.analysis: The passive preserves the named participants of The assessor rejected the appeal.
Combining the two claims with although presents an explicitly supplied concession.

examples.sentence: What the team needed was a longer trial.
examples.analysis: A pseudo-cleft foregrounds the requested remedy; it is not always pragmatically identical to neutral order.

contrasts.a: The witness decided to withdraw her statement.
contrasts.note: Both are grammatical, but the first reports a decision and the second a completed action; they are not equivalent.

exceptions: A grammatically successful transformation can legitimately change focus when the task asks for emphasis. A close-equivalence task must acknowledge that added effect rather than claim that nothing changes.

mistakes.problem: Original says some failed; rewrite says None passed.
mistakes.reason: At least one did not pass; this does not establish how many passed and remains compatible with nobody passing.

mistakes.problem: Original names the inspector; rewrite omits the agent from The file was examined.
mistakes.repair: The file was examined by the inspector.
mistakes.reason: Retain the named actor when the task requires all source information.

glossary.definition: The part of an expression affected by negation, focus or another operator.
glossary.example: only the clerk versus only the forms

glossary.definition: A conclusion that follows from a statement’s meaning if that statement is true.
glossary.example: She left entails that her leaving occurred.

modules.title: Suspicious but grammatical: context and register
modules.definition: A suspicious construction is one a learner expects to be wrong because it is unfamiliar, formal, informal or variable. A defensible judgement examines its licensing context and intended reading before applying a preferred rewrite.
foundation: A sentence can already be correct even when a memorised classroom rule predicts trouble. This is the person I spoke to uses standard preposition stranding. It was me uses an ordinary standard object-form complement after be, while it was I belongs to a more formal style. Neither familiarity nor personal preference decides every grammatical question. When a task offers no change, consider it seriously. Identify a rule actually broken in the stated context; do not assume the exercise setter must have hidden a fault.
intermediate: Marked word order can be fully grammatical. Rarely have we seen such detail uses inversion after a fronted negative-frequency adjunct. Only Aisha knew the code has no inversion because only modifies the subject, whereas Only after the briefing did Aisha know the code fronts a restrictive adjunct. Reported questions use their own structure: By whom the document was signed remains unknown contains an embedded interrogative functioning as subject; it is not a direct question requiring Was the document signed ...? The whole clause’s function determines the pattern.
advanced: Regional, register and contextual alternatives need explicit labels. The committee are divided is acceptable British member agreement. I have just finished and the American I just finished can both be standard in suitable contexts. Mandative should in They insisted that he should attend is standard British usage. Informal or ordinary object who does not become automatically wrong because the more formal whom exists. An editor can still choose a more formal variant for a specified purpose, but that decision should be described as an editorial preference rather than a correction of universal grammar.
expert: Some apparent anomalies depend on a different lexical sense. She is being difficult gives a temporary behavioural reading, so a blanket prohibition on progressive be or all stative expressions fails. The researcher effected a change uses a legitimate verb meaning brought about. Historical prescriptive slogans can be useful reminders in limited contexts, but a reliable analysis identifies those limits. In a formal examination practice item, avoid giving two standard variants and asking for the only correct one unless the convention or meaning is supplied. In open analysis, explain why no repair is necessary and offer an optional recast separately.

patterns.meaning: An unusual order may be required or licensed by a recognised construction.
A different preferred form does not automatically make the source incorrect.

examples.sentence: By whom the permit was issued remains uncertain.
examples.analysis: The embedded interrogative is the subject of remains; its internal order is defensible.

examples.sentence: The committee are considering their separate objections.
examples.analysis: Plural member reference is licensed in British English.

contrasts.b: Only after noon did Nida have the key.
contrasts.note: Both are grammatical; only has different attachment and the fronted adjunct licenses inversion in the second.

exceptions: A stated specialist or house-style rule can require one standard variant for that assignment. Explain its scope rather than extending it to all English.

mistakes.problem: Rarely we had encountered such delays.
mistakes.repair: Rarely had we encountered such delays.
mistakes.reason: Here rarely is a fronted negative-frequency adjunct and the formal pattern uses inversion.

mistakes.problem: She asked where did I work.
mistakes.reason: Ordinary formal embedded-question order differs from direct-question inversion.

glossary.definition: A construction differing from the neutral order for a recognised effect.
The defensibility of a form under its intended interpretation and situation.

modules.title: Paragraph editing and explicit editorial reasoning
modules.definition: Paragraph editing examines local sentence grammar together with reference, temporal relations and logical connections across the text. A successful edit preserves the author’s supportable message while making the expression accurate and clear.
foundation: Read a paragraph once for its intended message before repairing details. Identify the participants and events, then check whether pronouns, tense choices and connectors allow a reader to track them. The goal is not to make every verb share one tense. A current report can explain an earlier trial and a future recommendation. Nor must every paragraph use one voice. An active sentence may introduce an actor while a passive sentence continues discussion of the affected object. Explain a change in terms of the text’s information, not a general ban.
intermediate: Use a worked original paragraph. Draft: The library tested a new booking system last month. Its users was asked to reserve seats online, and several advice were posted near the desk. The report suggests that the system may reduce waiting, although only twelve visitors answered the survey. The team will collect more evidence before it makes a permanent decision. A restrained edit changes users was to users were and several advice were to several pieces of advice were. It keeps may, although and only twelve because those words limit the claim.
advanced: Classify each change. Users/were is agreement; pieces of advice repairs ordinary countability and preserves plurality through pieces; may is modal uncertainty; only twelve identifies a small response group without proving that no other visitors existed. Do not change suggests/may into proves/will merely to sound confident. The last sentence’s future form is compatible with the past trial and present report. Before it makes uses a present form in an ordinary future time clause. These relationships show why a grammatical paragraph can contain several time references.
expert: An editorial report should quote the problematic wording, explain the principle, give a corrected form and identify alternatives when meaningful. Other valid repairs of several advice include some advice was or several recommendations were; the choice changes how explicitly separate items are counted. A good rubric recognises those alternatives and requires preservation of the source’s caution. If a source passage is unclear, state the ambiguity and ask for its intended reference in a real editing workflow. In a self-study task, present conditional repairs rather than silently deciding who a pronoun means or inventing a missing cause.

patterns.form: paragraph meaning → local repairs → cross-sentence recheck
patterns.meaning: Protects the source’s central message during editing.
Makes a correction defensible and useful for revision.

examples.sentence: The users were asked to reserve seats online.
examples.analysis: Plural users controls were; the passive is appropriate because the users remain the topic.

examples.sentence: Several pieces of advice were posted near the desk.
examples.analysis: Pieces supplies countable units and plural agreement; advice remains uncountable.

examples.sentence: The report suggests that the system may reduce waiting.
examples.analysis: Present reporting and modal caution can coexist with an earlier past-time trial.

contrasts.a: The report suggests that the system may help.
contrasts.b: The report proves that the system will help.
contrasts.note: Both are well formed, but the second makes a much stronger evidential and future claim; it is not a faithful automatic edit.

exceptions: An editor can restructure substantially when the source permits several meanings, but must state the assumed interpretation. Minimum correction does not require preserving harmful ambiguity.

mistakes.problem: Its users was invited to respond.
mistakes.repair: Its users were invited to respond.
mistakes.reason: Plural subject users controls the passive auxiliary were.

mistakes.problem: The trial may helps some visitors.
mistakes.repair: The trial may help some visitors.
mistakes.reason: The modal selects a base-form lexical verb; some must remain if it limits the claim.

glossary.definition: A reason connecting an edit to grammar, meaning or stated style.
glossary.example: Changing was to were for plural users.

glossary.definition: A revision retaining the relevant source propositions and qualifications.

questions.prompt: What is the principal agreement fault in The quality of these reports have improved?
options: Quality is singular but have is plural here.
questions.why: Quality heads the subject; has is the conventional repair. Reports is inside its of-phrase.

questions.prompt: The source says some applications failed. Which rewrite preserves that without claiming universal failure?
questions.why: Not all permits both failure and some success; the other options exclude all success.

questions.prompt: Choose the genuine error: The committee are considering their separate views. Assume British member-oriented reference.
questions.why: The supplied member-oriented British context licenses plural agreement and reference.

questions.prompt: Which reconstruction retains the named actor in The assessor rejected the appeal?
options: The appeal was rejected by the assessor.
questions.why: The passive retains actor, action, affected appeal and past reference; other options omit or change a relevant feature.

questions.prompt: Why is She advised him to resign not equivalent to He resigned?
options: The first reports advice without entailing compliance.
questions.why: Giving advice does not entail that the advised action occurred.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct formal embedded subject clause.
options: By whom was the report signed remains unclear.
By whom did the report signed remains unclear.
By whom the report signed was remains unclear.
By whom the report was signed remains unclear.
questions.why: The embedded interrogative functions as subject of remains; ordinary uninverted internal order is appropriate.

questions.prompt: Which revision of The trial may reduce costs adds unsupported certainty?
options: Costs may be reduced by the trial.
A reduction in costs may result from the trial.
questions.why: Will asserts a stronger future commitment than the supplied possibility; the other options can retain possibility.

questions.prompt: Which is a genuine error in The findings was presented very clearly?
questions.why: Plural findings requires were; very clearly is an appropriate adverb phrase.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses only with the checker as its focus?
options: The clerk checked the only forms.
The clerk checked only the forms.
Only the clerk checked the forms.
The clerk only checked the forms, doing nothing else.
questions.why: Only the clerk restricts the subject; the other supplied readings focus the object or action.

questions.prompt: Which statement is accurate about an editing rubric?
options: It should permit different repairs that preserve the required meaning.
A revealed model objectively grades original prose.
Only the model’s exact wording can be correct.
questions.why: Open-ended editing permits defensible alternatives; model display is a self-review aid, not automated grading.

questions.prompt: Diagnose both faults: The findings was presented very clear to the visitors.
questions.model: Findings requires plural were; clear must be clearly for the intended manner of presentation.
alternatives: The findings were very clear to the visitors is grammatical but describes clarity of findings rather than presentation manner.

questions.prompt: Compare Not all visitors complained with No visitors complained.
questions.model: Not all denies universality and allows some complaints; no excludes complaints by every visitor.
rubric: Do not treat them as equivalent.
alternatives: Some visitors did not complain can paraphrase the first.

questions.prompt: Combine without inventing a cause: The alarm failed. The caretaker left early.
questions.model: The alarm failed, and the caretaker left early.
rubric: Do not use because or therefore without support.
alternatives: Accept a different response only if it preserves all stated propositions and satisfies the specific instruction, including supplied words, requested construction and sentence count. A grammatical recast that changes those constraints does not complete this task.

questions.prompt: Recast with provided that while preserving the condition and possibility: If the documents arrive today, we can finish the review tomorrow.
questions.model: The review can be finished tomorrow, provided that the documents arrive today.
alternatives: Provided that the documents arrive today, we can finish the review tomorrow. Do not turn a sufficient condition into an unsupported necessary condition.

questions.prompt: Order for the intended meaning of a restrictive opening: only after the inspection / the room / did / reopen.
questions.model: Only after the inspection did the room reopen.
rubric: Keep only after the inspection fronted.
Place did before subject and base-form reopen after.
alternatives: Accept a different response only if it preserves all stated propositions and satisfies the specific instruction, including supplied words, requested construction and sentence count. A grammatical recast that changes those constraints does not complete this task.

questions.prompt: Classify the issue: Amina told Salma that her proposal had been accepted. No wider context identifies her.
questions.model: Potential reference ambiguity, not an automatic structural error.
rubric: Do not invent the intended owner.
alternatives: Context may make either reading clear.

questions.prompt: Repair only the genuine grammatical fault: The department is comprised of four units and have a shared entrance.
questions.model: The department is comprised of four units and has a shared entrance.
rubric: Do not reject the established comprised of pattern.
alternatives: The department comprises four units and has a shared entrance is a valid recast.

questions.prompt: Explain why By whom the permit was signed remains unknown need not be corrected into direct-question order.
questions.model: By whom the permit was signed is an embedded interrogative functioning as the subject of remains; its internal subject precedes was.
rubric: Distinguish an independent question from an embedded clause.
alternatives: It remains unknown by whom the permit was signed is valid.

questions.prompt: Use suitable forms: The number of entries ____ risen, but several entries ____ still incomplete.
rubric: Distinguish singular number from plural entries.
Keep perfect auxiliary and be agreement separate.
alternatives: Had; were is valid only under an explicitly past-time framing.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between The witness decided to withdraw and The witness withdrew.
questions.model: A decision does not establish that withdrawal occurred; the second reports the event itself.
rubric: Identify the extra entailment in withdrew.
Avoid automatic compression that removes decided to.
alternatives: Planned/intended would require a suitably qualified source context.

questions.prompt: In The inspector found the procedure confusing, identify the function of confusing.
questions.model: It is an object complement describing the procedure.
rubric: Keep adjective/participle form separate from function.
alternatives: Predicative complement of the object is a valid modern label.

questions.prompt: Edit while preserving uncertainty: The trial lasted six weeks. Its findings was promising, but only ten visitor responded. The report suggest the change may helps.
questions.model: The trial lasted six weeks. Its findings were promising, but only ten visitors responded. The report suggests the change may help.
alternatives: Other complete reconstructions preserving the limits are valid.

questions.prompt: Why can a paragraph legitimately use tested, suggests and will collect in successive sentences?
questions.model: They can refer to a past trial, a current report and a future evidence-collection plan.
rubric: Do not require a single tense mechanically.
alternatives: The surrounding context must make those reference times coherent.

questions.prompt: Make a passive preserving the named agent and modality: The registrar may reject incomplete forms.
questions.model: Incomplete forms may be rejected by the registrar.
alternatives: Accept a different response only if it preserves all stated propositions and satisfies the specific instruction, including supplied words, requested construction and sentence count. A grammatical recast that changes those constraints does not complete this task.

questions.prompt: Evaluate the two sentences: It was me / It was I.
questions.model: Both are established; me is ordinary standard usage, while I is more formal and often marked.
rubric: Distinguish register rather than condemn ordinary me.
Do not use this complement pattern to justify object pronouns as ordinary subjects.
alternatives: I was the person involved can avoid the register contrast.

questions.prompt: Write an editorial note giving a conditional repair for ambiguous her in Amina told Salma that her proposal was accepted.
questions.model: If Amina owns it: Amina told Salma that Amina’s proposal was accepted. If Salma owns it: Amina told Salma that Salma’s proposal was accepted.
rubric: Do not silently choose an owner.
alternatives: Natural recasts using your/my are valid if the report perspective is made explicit.

questions.prompt: An editor changes some advice was posted to several pieces of advice were posted. What must be checked?
questions.model: The revised version explicitly counts separate pieces; ensure the source supports that plurality rather than merely an unspecified amount.
alternatives: Several recommendations were posted is valid if separate recommendations are intended.

questions.prompt: Write three lines for a genuine correction: original, principle, repair. Use your own example of auxiliary do with a lexical verb.
questions.model: Original: Did she attended? Principle: did carries past tense, so the lexical verb uses the base form. Repair: Did she attend?
alternatives: A negative pattern such as did not attended can be used.

corrections.prompt: Repair both faults: Several useful advices was included.
corrections.model: Several useful pieces of advice were included.
alternatives: Some useful advice was included is grammatical but leaves the count unspecified.

corrections.prompt: No change if grammatical: The committee have recorded their individual objections. Assume British member reference.
rubric: Do not invent a universal singular-only rule.
alternatives: The committee members have recorded their individual objections is explicit.

corrections.prompt: Repair: Having checked the figures, the analyst’s conclusion was revised. The analyst checked and revised it.
corrections.model: Having checked the figures, the analyst revised the conclusion.
rubric: Make analyst the understood checker and main-clause subject.
Retain both actions and supplied actor.
alternatives: After the analyst checked the figures, the analyst revised the conclusion. Preserve the supplied analyst as both checker and reviser.

corrections.prompt: Repair: Rarely the office had received such a detailed reply.
corrections.model: Rarely had the office received such a detailed reply.
alternatives: The office had rarely received such a detailed reply is valid.

corrections.prompt: No change if grammatical: They insisted that she should be consulted.
alternatives: They insisted that she be consulted is also valid.

corrections.prompt: The source states that some candidates succeeded, without saying whether others failed. Repair the inaccurate draft: No candidates succeeded.
rubric: Retain the explicitly supplied existence of successes.
Do not add failure, universality or an exact proportion that the source does not establish.
alternatives: Some of the candidates succeeded. Not all candidates succeeded requires evidence of at least one failure and is not licensed by this source alone.

corrections.prompt: Repair: The report suggest that the service may reduces waiting times.
corrections.model: The report suggests that the service may reduce waiting times.
alternatives: The report suggests a possible reduction in waiting times is a valid compression.

corrections.prompt: No change if grammatical: This is the file I was looking for.
rubric: Accept object relative omission and stranded for.
Do not require an artificially formal recast.
alternatives: This is the file for which I was looking is grammatical but marked.

transformations.prompt: Combine using a relative clause, preserving who owns the diary: I found a diary. The diary belonged to my aunt.
transformations.model: I found a diary that belonged to my aunt.
rubric: Use the relative to modify diary.
alternatives: I found a diary belonging to my aunt is valid.

transformations.prompt: Split without losing the concession: Although the proposal may reduce costs, the evidence is too limited to justify immediate adoption.
transformations.model: The proposal may reduce costs. However, the evidence is too limited to justify immediate adoption.
alternatives: Nevertheless can replace however; other accurate two-sentence versions are valid.

writing.prompt: Edit the library paragraph in Module4, then write a 100–140-word rationale identifying at least four relationships: agreement, countability, time reference and uncertainty. Include an alternative repair and explain any difference in meaning.
writing.model:
The library tested a new booking system last month. Its users were asked to reserve seats online, and several pieces of advice were posted near the desk. The report suggests that the system may reduce waiting, although only twelve visitors answered the survey. The team will collect more evidence before it makes a permanent decision.

Rationale: I first checked the subjects and finite verb phrases, because an attractive rewrite would not repair a basic agreement or auxiliary error. I then examined the clause boundaries and made the logical links explicit without inventing a new cause. The revision preserves the source’s limits on quantity and certainty: an observation about some users cannot establish a universal result. I also kept each pronoun’s intended referent recoverable and checked that modifiers attach to the people or events specified in the task. A different punctuation repair can be legitimate if it preserves those relationships and forms complete sentences. Finally, I separated recommendations from completed actions, since replacing one with the other would change the report rather than correct its grammar.
rubric: Repair genuine faults without erasing may/only twelve or inventing results.
Explain the four specified relationships accurately.
Give an alternative with a specific semantic or stylistic consequence.
Judge the rationale by evidence rather than exact model wording.
Keep the rationale itself within 100–140 words, separately from the repaired paragraph.
alternatives: Other valid paragraph repairs and reasoned alternatives are acceptable; do not infer unreported permanent success.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 25: Why can a judicial decision be grammatical even if it is not judicious?
recall.model: Judicial relates to courts; judicious evaluates wisdom.
rubric: Do not substitute an unsupported judgement.
alternatives: A court-related decision can be unwise.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 27: Why retain some and may in a précis?
recall.model: They limit the quantity and certainty of the original claim.
rubric: Avoid stronger universal or definite claims.
alternatives: Equivalent explanations using only or might can be valid with appropriate context.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 26: Why can repeating a precise technical term help cohesion?
recall.model: It maintains a stable referent and avoids a misleading synonym change.
rubric: Avoid claiming that every repetition is necessary.
alternatives: A clear pronoun can also maintain reference when unambiguous.

checklist: I can name the exact problematic relationship.
I check whether an unfamiliar construction is already grammatical.
I preserve negation, quantity, modality and named participants.
I identify more than one legitimate repair when context permits.
I can explain an edit without relying on a slogan.
